<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @outstaff/core run docs:schema`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The team config lives at `.outstaff/team.yaml` in your repository. For a prose tour of the sections, see [Team config](/concepts/team-config/). Problems found by `ost validate` are listed in [Validation codes](/reference/validation-codes/). The same schema is published as JSON Schema in `packages/core/schema/team.schema.json`.

Paths use `[]` for list items and `<key>` for a map entry whose key you choose.

## Example

A complete file for the synthetic team "acme".

```yaml
# Synthetic example: the "acme" team does not exist. All names, handles,
# addresses and URLs below are made up. It is used by tests and docs.

# Schema version of this file; currently 1.
version: 1

# Who the team is.
team:
  name: acme
  product: Acme Shop
  description: The team that builds and runs Acme Shop.

# Trusted humans. Optional; when omitted, trusted humans are repo writers and full chat-workspace members.
humans:
  - name: Ada Admin
    identities:
      vcs: ada-admin
      tracker: ada.admin
      chat: U0ADA0001
      email: ada@acme.example
  - name: Grace Lead
    identities:
      vcs: grace-lead
      chat: U0GRACE02

# Which catalog of roles and skills the team uses.
catalog:
  version: 0.0.0

# Repositories the team works in; at least one.
repos:
  - name: shop
    url: github.com/acme-example/shop
    kind: primary
    checks:
      - pnpm lint
      - pnpm vitest related --run
  - name: infra
    url: github.com/acme-example/infra
    kind: infra
  - name: design-system
    url: github.com/acme-example/design-system
    kind: baseline
  - name: docs-site
    url: github.com/acme-example/docs-site
    kind: other

# The agents on the team; may be empty.
people:
  - handle: priya
    name: Priya Raman
    pronouns: she/her
    role: pm
    identities:
      vcs: acme-priya[bot]
      chat: U0PRIYA03
      tracker: priya.raman
    repos:
      "*": read
      docs-site: write
  - handle: tomas
    name: Tomas Novak
    pronouns: he/him
    role: product
    identities:
      vcs: acme-tomas[bot]
      chat: U0TOMAS04
      tracker: tomas.novak
    repos:
      "*": read
      docs-site: write
  - handle: mira
    name: Mira Okafor
    pronouns: she/her
    role: architect
    extends: [developer]
    identities:
      vcs: acme-mira[bot]
      chat: U0MIRA005
      tracker: mira.okafor
    repos:
      shop: write
      "kind:baseline": read
  - handle: leo
    name: Leo Fischer
    pronouns: he/him
    role: designer
    identities:
      chat: U0LEO0006
      tracker: leo.fischer
  - handle: sam
    name: Sam Duarte
    pronouns: they/them
    role: developer
    identities:
      vcs: acme-sam[bot]
      chat: U0SAM0007
      tracker: sam.duarte
    repos:
      shop: write
      "kind:baseline": read
  - handle: noor
    name: Noor Haddad
    pronouns: she/her
    role: developer
    identities:
      vcs: acme-noor[bot]
      chat: U0NOOR008
      tracker: noor.haddad
    repos:
      shop: write
      "kind:baseline": read
  - handle: ines
    name: Ines Varga
    pronouns: she/her
    role: reviewer
    identities:
      vcs: acme-ines[bot]
      chat: U0INES009
      tracker: ines.varga
    repos:
      "*": read
  - handle: kofi
    name: Kofi Mensah
    pronouns: he/him
    role: devops
    identities:
      vcs: acme-kofi[bot]
      chat: U0KOFI010
      tracker: kofi.mensah
    repos:
      infra: write
      shop: read

# Which adapters connect Outstaff to your tools.
integrations:
  chat:
    adapter: slack
  vcs:
    adapter: github
  runtime:
    adapter: claude-agent-sdk
  tracker:
    adapter: itsaplan
    url: https://tracker.acme.example
    project: SHOP
  knowledge:
    adapter: itsaplan
  avatars:
    adapter: dicebear
    style: notionists

# How work moves through the team.
workflow:
  preset: kanban
  statuses:
    backlog: Backlog
    ready: Ready
    active: In Progress
    review: In Review
    blocked: Blocked
    done: Done
    canceled: Canceled

# Team-wide guardrails, message style and switches for what outstaff does on its own.
policies:
  # What outstaff does on its own. Everything below is on by default; set a switch to false (or none) to turn it off.
  acknowledge:
    chat: true
    vcs: true
  chat:
    profile: true
  design:
    canvas: true
  feedback:
    follow_up_round: true
    merged_prs: true
    doc_comments: true
    ticket_comments: true
    mentions: true
  hand_back:
    reassign: requester
    fallback: first_human
  tickets:
    prs_per_ticket: one
    start_moves_active: true
  conflicts:
    follow_up: true
  retry:
    on_signal: true
  messages:
    max_lines: 3
```

## Fields

## version

Schema version of this file; currently 1.

- Type: `number`
- Required
- Must be `1`

## team

Who the team is.

- Type: `object`
- Required

### team.name

Team slug: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 40
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`

### team.product

Name of the product the team builds.

- Type: `string`
- Optional

### team.description

One-line description of the team.

- Type: `string`
- Optional

## humans

Trusted humans. Optional; when omitted, trusted humans are repo writers and full chat-workspace members.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

## humans[]

A trusted human.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### humans[].name

Display name of the trusted human.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

### humans[].identities

How this human is known on each connected system; at least one is required.

- Type: `object`
- Required

#### humans[].identities.vcs

Username on the VCS host.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### humans[].identities.tracker

Username or id in the issue tracker.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### humans[].identities.chat

Username or id in the chat workspace.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### humans[].identities.email

Email address.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

## catalog

Which catalog of roles and skills the team uses.

- Type: `object`
- Required

### catalog.version

Exact catalog release this team uses, for example "1.0.0"; must match the catalog in the agent images.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

### catalog.path

Directory of ejected catalog files, relative to this file.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `catalog`
- Minimum length 1

## repos

Repositories the team works in; at least one.

- Type: `list of object`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

## repos[]

A repository the team works in.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### repos[].name

Short name used to refer to this repository in grants.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 40
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`

### repos[].url

Repository location: host/owner/repo, an https URL or a git@ address.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Must match `^(https?:\/\/\S+|git@\S+:\S+|[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\/[\w.-]+\/[\w.-]+)$`

### repos[].kind

Role of the repository: primary (the product, at most one), baseline, infra or other.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `primary`, `baseline`, `infra`, `other`

### repos[].default_branch

Branch that pull requests target.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `main`
- Minimum length 1

### repos[].checks

Commands an agent runs before pushing, covering only what a change affects (for example lint and the tests related to changed files). CI runs the full suite. When omitted, agents work out the affected checks themselves.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

### repos[].checks[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### repos[].conventions

How work is done in this repository, as free text: commits, branches, pull request title and body, tests. For repositories whose own files (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, the pull request template) cannot say it. Agents read it in addition to those files.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### repos[].ticket_link

Extra ways this repository's pull request body names its ticket, as regular expressions with one {key} placeholder for the ticket key (for example `Ticket: {key}`). A pull request is always linked by the ticket key in its branch name, its title, or a closing keyword in its body (`Closes ACME-12`); these patterns add to the last. A key mentioned in the body in any other way links nothing.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

### repos[].ticket_link[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 200

### repos[].instructions

Extra files in this repository that agents read before they work, relative to its root, for example ["CLAUDE.md"]. A project CLAUDE.md is not loaded into agent sessions unless it is listed here.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

### repos[].instructions[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### repos[].tracker

Which tracker tickets this repository serves. Agents use it to decide where a ticket's work goes when the ticket does not name a repository.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### repos[].tracker.labels

Ticket labels that mean the work belongs in this repository.

- Type: `list of string`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

#### repos[].tracker.labels[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

## people

The agents on the team; may be empty.

- Type: `list of object`
- Required

## people[]

An AI agent on the team.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### people[].handle

Unique lowercase handle; used as the agent's hostname label and mention name.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 30
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`

### people[].name

Display name of the agent.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

### people[].pronouns

Pronouns shown in the agent's profile.

- Type: `string`
- Optional

### people[].role

Catalog role this agent plays, for example "developer".

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

### people[].extends

Extra catalog roles or skill bundles layered on top of the role.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional

### people[].extends[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### people[].model

LLM model for this agent; the runtime adapter's default when omitted.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### people[].identities

How this agent is known on each connected system. The office recognizes the agent's own activity only by an exact match with these.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].identities.vcs

Login of this agent on the VCS host, for example "acme-sam[bot]".

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### people[].identities.tracker

Username or id of this agent in the issue tracker.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### people[].identities.chat

Username or id of this agent in the chat workspace.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### people[].repos

Repository access by repo name, "kind:<primary|baseline|infra|other>" or "*"; values are "read" or "write".

- Type: `map`
- Optional
- Default: `{}`

### people[].tools

Tools for this agent only; they replace team-level tools of the same name.

- Type: `map`
- Optional

#### people[].tools.<key>

A tool installed at agent start, with the commands it may run.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].tools.<key>.version

Exact version to install, for example "1.23.4".

- Type: `string`
- Required

#### people[].tools.<key>.source

Where mise gets the tool, as a mise backend and name such as ubi:vendor/their-cli or npm:their-cli. Defaults to the tool name, which mise looks up in its registry.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Must match `^[a-z0-9_-]+:\S+$`

#### people[].tools.<key>.allow

What the agent may run: "all" (any arguments), a list of first subcommands, or structured rules. Installing a tool allows nothing by itself. The built-in denies still win.

- Type: `string or list of string or list of object`
- Required

#### people[].tools.<key>.allow[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### people[].network

Network grants for this agent, merged over those of its roles.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].network.http

Services reachable with `ost http`.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

#### people[].network.http[]

A service the agent may reach with `ost http`.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].network.http[].name

Name the agent gives to `ost http`, for example hub.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 30
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`

#### people[].network.http[].url

Origin of the service, for example https://hub.acme.example.

- Type: `string`
- Required

#### people[].network.http[].token

Key of a secret in this person's secrets; sent as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` to this service. The agent never sees the value.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`

#### people[].network.adb

Devices reachable with `ost adb`.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

#### people[].network.adb[]

An Android device the agent may reach with `ost adb`.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].network.adb[].name

Name the agent gives to `ost adb`, for example test-tablet.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 30
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`

#### people[].network.adb[].host

Host name or IP address of the device, for example 10.0.0.16.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Maximum length 253
- Must match `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9.-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$`

#### people[].network.adb[].port

Fixed adb port, for example 5555 (adb over TCP). Omit for wireless pairing.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Minimum 1
- Maximum 65535

#### people[].network.adb[].pairing

Android 11+ wireless debugging: the connect port is random and changes, so a human supplies it. Use instead of port.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Must be `wireless`

#### people[].network.raw_http

Also let the agent run `curl` against the origins in `http`. Off by default. `curl` sends no token.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional

### people[].avatar

Avatar settings.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### people[].avatar.seed

Seed for a generated avatar.

- Type: `string`
- Optional

#### people[].avatar.url

Image URL to use as the avatar.

- Type: `string`
- Optional

Name of the adapter package to use, for example "github".

- Required

### integrations.knowledge

- Type: `object`

## email

Email addresses for agents.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### email.pattern

Address pattern for agents, for example "{handle}@acme.example".

- Type: `string`
- Required

## office

Office event intake settings.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### office.events

How the office learns about changes: polling or webhooks.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `poll`
- Allowed values: `poll`, `webhook`

### office.poll_interval_seconds

Seconds between polls when events is "poll".

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `60`
- Minimum 10
- Maximum 3600

### office.poll_warn_after_minutes

Minutes without a successful poll of an event source before the office logs a warning. Default 10.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Minimum 1
- Maximum 1440

### office.channel

Team chat channel where the office mirrors agent-to-agent questions and answers, so humans can follow them. Without it they go to the ticket of the asking work item, or only to its journal.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

## workflow

How work moves through the team.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### workflow.preset

Built-in workflow to start from.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `kanban`
- Allowed values: `kanban`, `scrum`, `minimal`

### workflow.statuses

Maps canonical statuses to the status names used in your tracker.

- Type: `map`
- Optional
- Allowed keys: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`

### workflow.rules

Rules added to the preset. A rule with a preset rule's id replaces it; { id, disabled: true } removes it.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

### workflow.rules[]

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### workflow.rules[].id

Unique id. A rule with the same id as a preset rule replaces it.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Maximum length 64
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`

#### workflow.rules[].on

Event type or types that trigger the rule.

- Type: `string or list of string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `pr.opened`, `pr.merged`, `pr.closed`, `pr.review_submitted`, `pr.comment`, `pr.conflicted`, `pr.ci_failed`, `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.moved`, `ticket.commented`, `ticket.created`, `doc.commented`, `agent.handed_back`, `agent.asked`, `schedule.cron`

#### workflow.rules[].on[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `pr.opened`, `pr.merged`, `pr.closed`, `pr.review_submitted`, `pr.comment`, `pr.conflicted`, `pr.ci_failed`, `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.moved`, `ticket.commented`, `ticket.created`, `doc.commented`, `agent.handed_back`, `agent.asked`, `schedule.cron`

#### workflow.rules[].if

Condition that must hold.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### workflow.rules[].if.all

- Type: `list of condition`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.all[]

- Type: `condition`
- Optional

#### workflow.rules[].if.any

- Type: `list of condition`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.any[]

- Type: `condition`
- Optional

#### workflow.rules[].if.not

- Type: `condition`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_status

- Type: `list of string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_status[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`

#### workflow.rules[].if.moved_to

- Type: `list of string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.moved_to[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`

#### workflow.rules[].if.actor_kind

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `human`, `agent`, `automation`

#### workflow.rules[].if.assignee_kind

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `human`, `agent`, `none`

#### workflow.rules[].if.has_label

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.pr_author_kind

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `human`, `agent`, `bot`

#### workflow.rules[].if.approver

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.pr_draft

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.pr_open

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.pr_merged

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.has_body

- Type: `boolean`

#### workflow.rules[].if.agent_mentioned

- Type: `list of string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `done`, `waiting`, `blocked`
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.hand_back_status[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `done`, `waiting`, `blocked`

#### workflow.rules[].if.hand_back_kind

- Type: `list of string`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.hand_back_kind[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### workflow.rules[].if.pr_approved

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_prs_all_closed

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_prs_open

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_prs_several

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].if.ticket_handed_back

- Type: `boolean`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].do

Actions, run in order.

- Type: `list of object`
- Required
- Minimum items 1

#### workflow.rules[].do[]

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### workflow.rules[].do[].move

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Allowed values: `backlog`, `ready`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].assign

Assign the ticket.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Must match `^(author|last_worker|requester|mentioned|none|human:\S+|role:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)$`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].comment

- Type: `string or object`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].do[].comment.template

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].comment.on

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `ticket`, `pr`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].schedule

- Type: `object`
- Required

#### workflow.rules[].do[].schedule.person

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Must match `^(author|assignee|last_worker|doc_author|mentioned|other_mentioned|role:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)$`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].schedule.kind

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`

#### workflow.rules[].do[].schedule.priority

- Type: `string`

- Allowed values: `low`, `normal`, `high`

#### workflow.rules[].disabled

Set to true to remove the rule.

### workflow.templates

Comment and notification templates by id, with {{variable}} placeholders. They override built-in templates with the same id.

- Type: `map`
- Optional

### workflow.needs_human_label

Ticket label that keeps work with a human. Default "needs-human".

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

## policies

Team-wide guardrails, message style and switches for what outstaff does on its own.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

### policies.agent_loop_guard

Stops agents from triggering each other in endless loops. Limits only runs triggered by agents or automation; humans are never limited.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"max_runs_per_item_per_hour":12}`

#### policies.agent_loop_guard.max_runs_per_item_per_hour

Maximum runs per work item per hour triggered by agents or automation; humans are never limited.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `12`
- Minimum 1

### policies.usage

Thresholds that slow down work as the LLM usage limit approaches.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"defer_scheduled_at":0.85,"pause_automatic_at":0.95}`

#### policies.usage.defer_scheduled_at

Fraction of the usage limit at which scheduled work is deferred.

- Type: `number`
- Optional
- Default: `0.85`
- Minimum 0
- Maximum 1

#### policies.usage.pause_automatic_at

Fraction of the usage limit at which all automatic work pauses.

- Type: `number`
- Optional
- Default: `0.95`
- Minimum 0
- Maximum 1

#### policies.usage.shared

Groups of people who use one LLM subscription, as lists of handles. A usage report from any member applies to all of them.

- Type: `list of list of string`
- Optional

#### policies.usage.shared[]

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 2

#### policies.usage.shared[][]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### policies.acknowledge

The reactions that show people their message or comment was picked up.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"chat":true,"vcs":true}`

#### policies.acknowledge.chat

React with eyes to a chat message from a trusted person when the agent has seen it. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.acknowledge.vcs

React with eyes to each pull request comment the agent is about to answer, when its round starts. Needs a vcs adapter with vcs.reactions. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.feedback

How agents act on feedback from trusted people beyond the first round.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"follow_up_round":true,"merged_prs":true,"doc_comments":true,"ticket_comments":true,"mentions":true}`

#### policies.feedback.follow_up_round

Start another round when feedback arrived after the agent was offered its work. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.feedback.merged_prs

Schedule the author to answer feedback on a merged pull request. Switches the preset rule merged-feedback-follow-up. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.feedback.doc_comments

Schedule the author of a knowledge document to answer a trusted person's comments on it. Switches the preset rule doc-feedback-to-author. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.feedback.ticket_comments

Start a round for the assigned agent when a trusted person comments on its ticket, and send a handed-back ticket back to its last worker. Switches the preset rules ticket-comment-to-assignee and ticket-comment-reactivates-ticket. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.feedback.mentions

Hand a ticket to the agent a trusted person mentions in a comment on it (assign, move to active, start a round), and start a round for an agent mentioned in a document comment. Switches the preset rules mention-assigns-agent, doc-mention-feedback and doc-mention-assigns-ticket. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.hand_back

What happens to a ticket when an agent hands its work back.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"reassign":"requester","blocked_notify":"pm","fallback":"first_human"}`

#### policies.hand_back.reassign

Who an agent's hand-back assigns the ticket to: the requester, or none to leave the assignee alone (the ticket still moves: to review when done, to blocked when blocked). Edits the preset rules hand-back-to-requester and hand-back-blocked-to-requester. Default requester.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `requester`
- Allowed values: `requester`, `none`

#### policies.hand_back.blocked_notify

Who deals with a blocked hand-back: pm schedules an unblock round for the team's PM, who messages the requester only if a human is needed; agent has the blocked agent tell the requester itself, in its own direct message. Without a PM role the agent always does. The office never posts to people. Default pm.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `pm`
- Allowed values: `pm`, `agent`

#### policies.hand_back.fallback

Who stands in when a ticket has no known requester: the first human in humans, or none to skip. Default first_human.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `first_human`
- Allowed values: `first_human`, `none`

### policies.tickets

How tickets and pull requests relate.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"prs_per_ticket":"one","start_moves_active":true}`

#### policies.tickets.prs_per_ticket

How many pull requests a ticket may have. one: ost pr open refuses a second one for a ticket and the ticket moves to done when its pull request merges; many: several are allowed and the ticket moves to done when the agent hands its work back as done and every pull request linked to it is closed with at least one merged. Edits the preset rules pr-merged-done, pr-closed-ready, hand-back-to-requester and second-pr-comment. Default one.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Default: `one`
- Allowed values: `one`, `many`

#### policies.tickets.start_moves_active

Move a ticket to active when a work item about it starts (assigned, ticket comment), if it is in backlog, ready, review or blocked. Rounds that only answer something (asked, document feedback) and chat sessions never move it, and the minimal preset never moves tickets. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.conflicts

Merge conflicts between pull requests.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"follow_up":true}`

#### policies.conflicts.follow_up

Send a pull request that starts to conflict with its base, for example after another one merged, back to its agent author to rebase. Switches the preset rule conflict-back-to-author. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.retry

How a failing work item is retried: exponential backoff, then blocked; and whether a human's signal brings a blocked item back.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"on_signal":true,"base_minutes":1,"cap_minutes":30,"max_failures":3}`

#### policies.retry.on_signal

Retry a blocked work item when a trusted human moves its ticket, assigns it, reviews or comments on its pull request, or replies in its chat thread. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.retry.base_minutes

Wait after the first failed run of a work item; doubles with each failure.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `1`
- Minimum 1

#### policies.retry.cap_minutes

Longest wait between two attempts at a failing work item.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `30`
- Minimum 1

#### policies.retry.max_failures

Consecutive failed runs after which the work item is blocked.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `3`
- Minimum 1

### policies.merge

Merging an agent's pull request when an allowed approver approves it (opt-in).

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"on_approval":false,"approvers":["humans"]}`

#### policies.merge.on_approval

Let an agent merge its own pull request, with ost pr merge, when an allowed approver approves it. Off by default: without it the verb refuses and nothing is scheduled. Adds the preset rules approved-merge and approved-merge-after-feedback. Needs a vcs adapter with vcs.merge. It never bypasses branch protection or rulesets; the code host stays the final gate.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `false`

#### policies.merge.approvers

Who may approve a merge: humans (the people in humans, or anyone with write access when humans is omitted), human:<id> (one human, by vcs identity), role:<role> (the agent playing a catalog role) or a handle (an agent, or a human by vcs login). Default humans.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Default: `["humans"]`
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.merge.approvers[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Must match `^(humans|human:\S+|role:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._[\]-]*)$`

#### policies.merge.method

How the pull request is merged: queue (the host's merge queue), merge or squash. When omitted, outstaff uses what the repository has: its merge queue, else a method its settings allow.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `queue`, `merge`, `squash`

#### policies.merge.repos

Names of the repos (from repos) whose pull requests may be merged this way. Default: every repo an agent can write to.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.merge.repos[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

### policies.messages

How agents write chat messages.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"max_lines":3,"always_link":true,"omit":["ci","mergeability","hashes"]}`

#### policies.messages.max_lines

Guidance for agents: keep chat replies to about this many lines. It is a hard limit only for the office's own automatic notices (status lines, run notifications). An agent's reply is never cut; one over a high safety cap is split into several messages.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `3`
- Minimum 1
- Maximum 20

#### policies.messages.always_link

Link tickets, pull requests and documents instead of mentioning bare ids.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

#### policies.messages.omit

Details left out of chat messages.

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Default: `["ci","mergeability","hashes"]`
- Allowed values: `ci`, `mergeability`, `hashes`, `file_lists`

#### policies.messages.omit[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `ci`, `mergeability`, `hashes`, `file_lists`

### policies.design

What design roles may use.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"canvas":true}`

#### policies.design.canvas

Let roles that declare the design.canvas capability use Claude's Artifact tools (the Design canvas). Needs the claude-agent-sdk runtime signed in with a Claude account. Default on; it does nothing for a role without the capability.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.chat

How agents take chat messages, and what they show in chat.

- Type: `object`
- Optional
- Default: `{"parallel_sessions":2,"profile":true}`

#### policies.chat.parallel_sessions

How many chat sessions an agent runs at once, beside its active work item. A message beyond that waits for a free session.

- Type: `integer`
- Optional
- Default: `2`
- Minimum 1
- Maximum 10

#### policies.chat.profile

Publish the agent's profile in chat: role, status, and current work grouped by ticket or pull request. Needs a chat adapter with chat.agentProfile. Default on.

- Type: `boolean`
- Optional
- Default: `true`

### policies.commands

Extra commands for this team's own tools, on top of the built-in and toolset rules.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.allow

Commands agents may run.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.allow[]

A command rule.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.allow[].program

Program name, for example make. Git is governed by repository grants.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Must match `^[^\s/]+$`

#### policies.commands.allow[].subcommand

Leading positional words, for example ["pr", "view"].

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.commands.allow[].subcommand[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### policies.commands.allow[].args

Every condition must hold for the rule to apply.

- Type: `list of any`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.commands.allow[].args[]

A condition on the command arguments.

- Type: `any`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.allow[].reason

Why the rule exists; shown when it decides a call.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

#### policies.commands.allow[].requires_repo

The working repository must have at least this grant.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `read`, `write`

#### policies.commands.deny

Commands agents may never run. Deny always wins over allow.

- Type: `list of object`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.deny[]

A command rule.

- Type: `object`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.deny[].program

Program name, for example make. Git is governed by repository grants.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1
- Must match `^[^\s/]+$`

#### policies.commands.deny[].subcommand

Leading positional words, for example ["pr", "view"].

- Type: `list of string`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.commands.deny[].subcommand[]

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Minimum length 1

#### policies.commands.deny[].args

Every condition must hold for the rule to apply.

- Type: `list of any`
- Optional
- Minimum items 1

#### policies.commands.deny[].args[]

A condition on the command arguments.

- Type: `any`
- Optional

#### policies.commands.deny[].reason

Why the rule exists; shown when it decides a call.

- Type: `string`
- Required
- Minimum length 1

#### policies.commands.deny[].requires_repo

The working repository must have at least this grant.

- Type: `string`
- Optional
- Allowed values: `read`, `write`
